entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2 Appellants are the 'B and H' claimants in L.A.R No.52 of 2014 on the file of Additional Sub Court,
North Paravur.
Respondents herein are the respondents 1 and 2 and claimants C, D, E, F, G, H1 and H2 as per the party array before the reference court.
By the impugned judgment and decree, the reference court dismissed the reference under Section 28A(3) of the Land Acquisition Act.
Heard the learned Counsel for the appellants and the learned Senior Government Pleader.
Perused the impugned judgment.

2. Landed properties having an extent of 0.18 Ares in Re-Sy.No.213/3-4-9 and having an extent of 2.70 Ares in Sy.No.207/4-1-17 of Karukutty Village were acquired from one Smt. Plamena, pursuant to a notification dated 24.07.2010, issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act for the construction of a Railway over-bridge.
The Land Acquisition Office fixed the land value at Rs.3,20,730/- per Are.

The owner of the properties died and her son and daughter-in-law, the appellants herein, made an application under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act relying LA.APP. NO. 404 OF 2017 2026:KER:29193 on a common judgment of the Sub Court, Paravur in L.A.R Nos. 7 of 2012, 8 of 2012 and 9 of 2012, dated 08.07.2013.

entities.text: L.A.R Nos. 7 of 2012, 8 of 2012 and 9 of 2012
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The application for enhancement was rejected.
Therefore, they approached the Sub Court under Section 28A(3) of the Land Acquisition Act.

According to the appellants the properties acquired from their predecessor in interest and the properties involved Exhibit A1 common judgment in L.A.R Nos. 7 of 2012, 8 of 2012 and 9 of 2012 are similarly situated and identical.

entities.text: L.A.R Nos. 7 of 2012, 8 of 2012 and 9 of 2012
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: They pointed out that the properties covered by Exhibit A1 judgment was also in Category No.I.
It is also pointed out that the reference court, in Exhibit A1 judgment, enhanced the land value to Rs.3,07,356/- per Are and hence they are also entitled for parity in compensation.
3. Heard the learned Counsel for the appellant and the learned Senior Government Pleader.
The learned Counsel for the appellant submitted that the reference court was wrong in rejecting the reference under Section 28A(3) of the Act.

The learned Sub Judge held that barring the oral testimony of AW1 no evidence was available to prove that the lands in the reference and the lands mentioned in Exhibit A1 judgment were similarly LA.APP. NO. 404 OF 2017 2026:KER:29193 situated or possessed of the same value of potentialities.

The learned Counsel for the appellant submitted that in a reference under Section 28A(3) of the Act, there is no necessity to adduce evidence of high standard relied on State of Kerala V. Indira Amma [2014 (1) KLT Suppl. 98 (Ker)].

entities.text: State of Kerala V. Indira Amma [2014 (1) KLT Suppl. 98 (Ker)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in the said case that in a reference under Section 28A (3), the claimant can only seek equal value as under the award passed by the Reference Court and no enquiry over any enhanced claim over the award under reference is permissible.
Further it was held that, the reference under Section 28A (3) no enquiry for enhancing compensation, contemplated under Section 18 of Act can be made.

It was also held that if the reference is made under Section 18 of the Act on the protest of land owner over the land value fixed and awarded for the acquired land by the Collector, the interested land owner can produce materials and substantiate his claim for enhanced land value.
However, no such enquiry is contemplated under Section 28A (3) of the Act.

4. The learned Sub Judge rejected the claim for the sole reason that, there was no evidence other than the interested testimony of AW1 to show that the properties involved in Exhibit LA.APP. NO.
404 OF 2017 2026:KER:29193 A1 and the properties involved in the instant case are identical.

However, it is to be noted that Exhibits R1 and R2 would show that the Land Acquisition Officer had Davis G.V vs State Of Kerala on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174250567/
3 fixed the land value of the properties acquired from the predecessor of the appellants at Rs.3,20,730/- per Are.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The same value was fixed for the properties involved in L.A.R Nos.7 of 2012,
8 of 2012 and 9 of 2012 also by the Land Acquisition Officer.

entities.text:
L.A.R Nos.7 of 2012,
8 of 2012 and 9 of 2012
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: This shows that the Land Acquisition Officer had treated the properties involved in Exhibit A1 judgment as also the properties acquired from the predecessor in the interest of the appellants as identical or as having the same value and potentialities.
The said aspect was overlooked by the learned Sub Judge by holding that there was no material available to show that the properties are identical.
In my considered view, the above aspect would clearly show that the properties were identical, as the Land Acquisition Officer had fixed the land value at the same rate.
Therefore, I am of the view that the learned Sub Judge ought to have decided the reference under Section 28A (3) in favour of the appellants.
Accordingly, the impugned judgment and decree are set aside.
The land value of the properties acquired from the LA.APP. NO. 404 OF 2017 2026:KER:29193 predecessor in interest of the appellants
is re -
fixed at Rs.3,07,356/- per Are.
The appellants shall be entitled or all statutory benefits also.
In view of Exhibit A2 Will, the 1 st appellant shall be entitled for compensation for 0.18 Ares and the 2 nd appellant shall be entitled for compensation for 2.70 Ares.
The appeal is allowed as above.
